How long does renewal take?Online, in most cases

components.docs:
Sections that open and close, for frequently asked questions and long guidance. Built on
native `<details>` and `<summary>`: they open with Enter or Space, expose their expanded
state to assistive technology and work before (and without) JavaScript. The component adds
the v2 look (ruled sections, a title-medium summary, a chevron at the end that turns over
when open) and an optional "Show all sections" toggle.

v2 renders in light DOM (Stencil `scoped`, architecture §3.1): the `<details>` stay your
own markup, so in-page links and `id`s inside them work as usual.

Put the question in `<summary>` as plain text, optionally followed by a `<small>` summary
line; put the answer after it. Keep headings out of `<summary>`: it is a button, so a
heading inside it is not announced as one.

# sc-account-menu

The signed-in account control for `sc-site-header`'s `slot="account"`: notifications with the unread count, and a disclosure with profile, settings, representation and sign out. Spec: `specs/sc-account-menu.md`.

## Usage

```html
<sc-account-menu slot="account" name="Sara Al Mansoori" acting-for="Al Mansoori Trading LLC"
  profile-href="/en/profile" settings-href="/en/settings" representation-href="/en/act-for"
  notifications-href="/en/notifications" unread="3"></sc-account-menu>
```

- Without `sign-out-href`, Sign out is a button that fires `scSignOut`: post your sign-out form from the listener.
- The initials come from the name as written; `initials` overrides them.
components.docs:
The signed-in account control in `sc-site-header` (`slot="account"`; component-language
B3, Standard CHR-01). It replaces "Sign in with UAE PASS" once the user is signed in.

- A notifications button (a link to the notifications page) with the unread count, named
  "Notifications, 3 unread".
- A `<button aria-expanded>` with the user's initials (and name from 1280px) that opens a
  non-modal panel: the name and who they are acting for, links to Profile, Settings and
  representation ("Change who you act for"), and Sign out.

The panel is a disclosure, not an ARIA menu: Tab moves through its links, Escape closes it
and returns focus to the button, a press outside or focus leaving closes it. From a
pointer it grows from the button's corner; from the keyboard it appears instantly.

# sc-announcement-bar

A site-wide announcement above the header (after the skip link). Spec: `specs/sc-announcement-bar.md`.

## Usage

```html
<sc-announcement-bar dismissible announcement-id="maintenance-2026-10-25"
  link-href="/en/status" link-text="See affected services">
  Planned maintenance on Saturday 25 October. Payment services will be unavailable from 2am to 6am (Dubai time).
</sc-announcement-bar>
```

- `tone`: `warning` (default), `info` or `error`. Say the severity in the words too.
- It is a labelled region present at load, not an alert. Change `announcement-id` when the message changes.
components.docs:
A site-wide announcement above the header: planned maintenance, a service outage, a change
people need to know about (component-language B1). One message, one optional link, and an
optional dismiss button.

A labelled region ("Announcement" / "إعلان"), present when the page loads. It is not a
live region and not an alert. The text carries the severity in words ("Planned
maintenance…"); the tone's icon and container repeat it.

Dismissing it fires `scDismiss` (cancelable) and hides it. With `announcement-id`, the
dismissal is remembered in this browser, so the same announcement does not come back.
Focus moves to the next focusable element after it. From a pointer it fades out over
`duration-exit`; from the keyboard it goes at once. Its height is never animated (MOT-11).

# sc-app-bar

The transaction app bar: the bar at the top of every step of a journey (component-language A4). Channel pages outside a transaction use `sc-site-header`. Spec: `specs/sc-app-bar.md`.

## Usage

```html
<sc-app-bar sticky>
  <sc-back-link slot="start" href="/en/renew-vehicle-registration/vehicle"></sc-back-link>
  <sc-language-switch slot="end" href="/ar/renew-vehicle-registration/plate"></sc-language-switch>
</sc-app-bar>
```

- `align="start"` and `shape="floating"` (v1's desktop header) are deprecated: use `sc-site-header`.
components.docs:
The transaction app bar (component-language A4; Standard TPL-01, LANG-04): the bar at the
top of every step of a journey (E2–E4). Channel pages outside a transaction use
`sc-site-header` instead.

A 4px rule in `channel-action` along the top; a start slot (the back link), the title (a
10px channel swatch and the channel name, centred) and an end slot (the language switch),
with fixed 96px side slots so the title stays centred; a 1px `outline-variant` rule
beneath. 60px tall on `surface`. Flat: no glass, no shadow.

with `sticky`, `sc-page sync-document` sets `scroll-padding-top` so focus never slides
under it (WCAG 2.4.11).

# sc-back-link

"Back" to the previous step, on every step of a journey except the first. Spec: `specs/sc-back-link.md`.

```html

# sc-button

Starts an action. If it goes somewhere instead, use `sc-link` (or `sc-button href` for a call to action that must look like a button, such as "Start now").

## Usage

```html
<sc-button type="submit" icon="arrow-forward">Continue</sc-button>
<sc-button variant="secondary">Save and finish later</sc-button>
<sc-button href="/renew/start" icon="arrow-forward">Start now</sc-button>
```

### Which variant

| Variant | Use it for | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `primary` | The one main action on the page. Never more than one per page or section. | "Continue", "Pay with Dubai Pay" |
| `secondary` | Other actions next to a primary one, or the main action when it isn't the way forward. | "Save and finish later", "Change" |
| `tertiary` | Low-emphasis actions that would compete with the primary if they had a fill. | "Cancel", "View all services" |
| `destructive` | An action that deletes data or can't be undone. Confirm it on the next screen. | "Delete draft", "Cancel renewal" |
| `handoff` | A shared government hand-off. City indigo on every channel, so it never looks like the channel's own action (U3). | "Sign in with UAE PASS", "Pay with Dubai Pay" |

- Heights follow the variant: 56px for `primary`, `destructive` and `handoff`; 48px for `secondary` and `tertiary`. Set `size="l"` (56px) or `size="m"` (48px) to override; `size="xl"` (64px) is for the hero search only.
- Use `full-width` on narrow screens when the button ends a form.
- Put the primary button first in the reading order. In Arabic it sits on the right automatically.

### Content

- Start with a verb and say what happens: "Continue", "Pay with Dubai Pay", "Save and finish later". Not "Submit", "OK" or "Click here".
- Sentence case, no full stop, as short as it can be while staying specific. Write the Arabic label, don't machine-translate it.
- Use the `arrow-forward` icon at the end only for actions that move the user forward in a journey. It mirrors in Arabic. Don't add icons for decoration.
- Amounts and references inside a label stay left-to-right: `<sc-button>Pay <sc-ltr>AED 450.00</sc-ltr></sc-button>`.

### States

- **Loading:** set `loading` while the action runs (for example, while a payment starts). The button keeps its width, shows a spinner, sets `aria-busy`, announces "Pay with Dubai Pay, Loading" (or the Arabic equivalent) and ignores clicks. Remove `loading` when the action ends.
- **Disabled:** supported, but avoid it. A disabled button can't be focused and gives no reason, so many users can't tell why they're stuck. Leave it enabled and show an error message (and `sc-error-summary`) when the user tries to continue.

### Forms

`sc-button` renders a native `<button>` (or `<a>`) in light DOM (v2, decision A2), so it is a real form control:

- `type="submit"` submits the surrounding `<form>`, and the first submit button is the form's **default button**: Enter in any field submits through it. `name`, `value` and `form="<form id>"` work as on a native button. `type="reset"` resets the form. The default `type` is `button`, unlike the native element.
- A `<fieldset disabled>` disables it natively.
- `focus()` and `click()` on the host reach the native control.
- There is no `::part()` in v2. Style overrides, if you must, target `.sc-button`, `.sc-button__label` and `.sc-button__icon`; the component's rules are in `@layer sc.components`, so your unlayered CSS wins.
- Frameworks that own children (React) must not re-render the label text after upgrade: Stencil moves it into the native button.

# sc-callout

An important message inside the page content: something the user must know before they act, or the result of what they just did. If the message is about errors in the user's answers, use `sc-error-summary` and field errors instead. If it's the status of a task or payment in a list, use `sc-status-tag`.

## Usage

```html
<sc-callout tone="warning">
  If your payment is interrupted, don't pay again. Check the payment status in My tasks first.
</sc-callout>

<sc-callout tone="success" heading="Registration renewed" heading-level="2">
  Your vehicle registration is valid until 18 October 2027.
</sc-callout>
```

### Which tone

| Tone | Use it for | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `info` (default) | Guidance the user needs. | "You'll need your plate number and Emirates ID number." |
| `success` | Something worked. | "We've sent the receipt to your email." |
| `warning` | Something the user must know to avoid a problem. | "If your payment is interrupted, don't pay again…" |
| `error` | Something went wrong that isn't about their answers. | "Your payment didn't go through. No money has been taken." |

v2: a tone-95 container with 8px corners, a tone-40 accent bar at inline-start (3px, `--sc-size-border-accent`) and icon, and the text in `on-surface`. Links inside keep the channel link colour. Each tone has its own fill, its own icon and a visually hidden word read before the message ("Warning:" / "تنبيه:"), so the meaning never relies on colour. Override the word with `tone-label` if a different one fits better.

### Content

- One callout per section at most; if everything is highlighted, nothing is.
- Lead with what the user should do or know. Short sentences, sentence case. Write the Arabic, don't translate word for word.
- `heading` is optional bold text. It is a plain paragraph by default; set `heading-level` (2–6) only when the heading belongs in the page outline. Use the `heading` slot for rich content.
- Inline links and `<sc-ltr>` for amounts and references are fine in the message.

# sc-checkbox

A checkbox: an option in `sc-checkbox-group`, or one box on its own for a single statement people must confirm, such as "I confirm the vehicle details are correct".

## Usage

```html
<sc-checkbox name="confirm" value="yes" required>I confirm the vehicle details are correct</sc-checkbox>
```

- The content is the label. Keep it short; put detail in `hint` (or a `slot="hint"` child, moved into place once).
- 24px box inside a 44px target: the whole label row is clickable. Space toggles it. The tick is a symbol, so it never mirrors in Arabic.
- **On its own:** `error` shows the error bar, the message with "Error:" and `aria-invalid`. `required` reports `valueMissing` until it's checked.
- **In a group:** the group shows the error and passes it down; the box submits its `value` under the group's `name` unless it has its own `name`.
- v2 renders a native `<input type="checkbox">` in light DOM (decision A2): it submits `value` (default `on`) when checked, resets to its initial `checked`, follows `<fieldset disabled>`, and `required` is native `valueMissing`. The native `change` bubbles; `scChange` carries `{ checked, value }`.
- The check draws over 120ms when toggled with a pointer and appears at once from the keyboard (MOT-02).

# sc-checkbox-group

Several choices from a short list: "Which documents do you have?", "Send reminders by". Use `sc-radio-group` when only one answer is allowed. For a single yes/no statement ("I confirm the vehicle details are correct") use one `sc-checkbox` on its own.

## Usage

```html
<sc-checkbox-group name="documents" label="Which documents do you have?" hint="Select all that apply">
  <sc-checkbox value="insurance">Valid insurance policy</sc-checkbox>
  <sc-checkbox value="inspection" hint="From a centre approved by RTA">Technical inspection certificate</sc-checkbox>
  <sc-checkbox value="fines">Receipt for paid fines</sc-checkbox>
</sc-checkbox-group>
```

- Legend, hint, `optional`, `error`, `inline`, `heading-level` and `disabled` work as in `sc-radio-group`.
- Say "Select all that apply" in the hint. Order options logically; don't pre-check options for people.
- **Error:** set `error` on the group. The group shows the bar and message; every box gets the error border and `aria-invalid`. The boxes' own `error` is ignored inside a group.

### Structure (v2, light DOM)

The group renders a native `<fieldset>`, `<legend>`, hint and error in light DOM (decision A2) and moves its `sc-checkbox` children inside the fieldset, so they are grouped and named by the legend natively. Each `sc-checkbox` renders its own native `<input type="checkbox">`, `<label>` and hint, so it also works on its own. `disabled` disables the fieldset, and with it every box. The group passes its `name` and error state to each box. Boxes appended later are moved in too.

### Forms

Each checked box submits its own `value` under the group's `name` (or its own `name`): `documents=insurance&documents=fines`, as native checkboxes do. Reset restores each box. With `required`, the first enabled box carries a native validity error ("Select at least one option") until one is checked, so `checkValidity()` and `reportValidity()` work. The native `change` bubbles from each box; `scGroupChange` carries `{ value: string[] }`.

# sc-date-input

A date people know: a date of birth, the start date on an insurance policy, the date a vehicle was exported. Don't use it for a date people need to pick from a calendar (an appointment): that needs a date picker.

## Usage

```html
<sc-date-input
  name="insuranceStart"
  label="When does your insurance policy start?"
  hint="For example, 27 3 2026"
></sc-date-input>
```

- Three labelled boxes, Day, Month and Year (يوم / شهر / سنة), in a `<fieldset>` with the question as the `<legend>`. Each box uses the numeric keyboard (`inputmode="numeric"`).
- **In Arabic** the boxes run right to left: Day on the right, Year on the left. Digits stay Latin.
- **Hint:** give an example in the order of the boxes: "For example, 27 3 2026".
- **Error on one part:** set `error` and `error-parts` to the boxes it's about, for example `error-parts="year"` with "The date your policy starts must include a year". Only those boxes get the error border and `aria-invalid`. Without `error-parts`, the error highlights all three.
- **Date of birth:** `autocomplete="bday"` sets `bday-day`, `bday-month`, `bday-year` on the boxes.
- `optional`, `heading-level` and `disabled` work as in the other fields.

### Value and forms

- `value` is an ISO date (`2026-03-27`). It's empty while the boxes don't make a real date (31 April, a 2-digit year). Setting `value` fills the boxes.
- The form gets the ISO date under `name`, plus the raw parts as `name-day`, `name-month` and `name-year`, so the server can validate and re-display exactly what was typed.
- v2 renders a native fieldset, three native inputs (named `name-day`, `name-month`, `name-year`) and a hidden input carrying the ISO date under `name`, in light DOM (decision A2).
- Validity: a native custom validity error on the Day box ("Enter a date") when `required` and every box is empty, and on the first empty box ("The date must be a real date") when something is typed but it isn't a real date. `reportValidity()` focuses that box. Reset restores the initial `value`.
- `scInput` and `scChange` carry `{ value, day, month, year }`. `focus()` on the host is forwarded to the Day box, so an error summary can focus the field by its `id`. The native `change` bubbles from each box.

# sc-date-range

A start and an end date that relate to a calendar: filtering payments or fines between two dates, the nights of a stay on Visit Dubai, how long a permit lasts. For a single date people already know (a date of birth, a policy start date), use `sc-date-input`: people type those faster than they find them in a calendar.

## Usage

```html
<sc-date-range
  name="payments"
  label="Show payments between"
  hint="For example, 21 9 2026"
  start="2026-09-21"
  end="2026-10-09"
  max="2026-10-19"
  max-days="365"
  presets
></sc-date-range>
```

- **Field:** a `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`, the hint, then one 56px frame with two typed segments, From and To (من / إلى), an arrow between them (→, ← in Arabic) and a calendar button at inline-end. People can always type: "21/9/2026", "21 9 2026" and "21-09-2026" all work, and each segment is formatted on blur ("21 Sep 2026").
- **Picker:** the calendar button opens a popover on medium and wider screens: one or two months (`months`, `auto` shows two from 720px), always 6 weeks, Monday first, and optional presets at inline-start. The first click sets the start, the second the end; a day before the start, or any day after a complete range, starts again. Apply writes both dates, closes the picker and returns focus to the button; Escape or a click outside closes without changes. Focus goes to the heading (or the first control with `initial-focus="first"`) and returns to the trigger on close. - Escape, the close button and the scrim close it (`scClose` says why). `alert` makes it an `alertdialog`: the scrim doesn't close it and there is no close button; Escape still does. - `countdown` (seconds) shows "Time left: 1:45" and announces it politely once on open, at each whole minute and at 30 and 10 seconds, never every second. `scCountdownEnd` fires at zero; nothing is submitted. A modal dialog for a short secondary task or a decision that can't wait, such as the
session-timeout warning (TIME-02). On phones (under 600px) the same component is a bottom
sheet.

It is a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`, so the page behind is inert and focus
can't leave it. On open, focus goes to the heading (or, with `initial-focus="first"`, the
first control). Escape, the close button and a click on the scrim close it (an `alert`
dialog ignores the scrim and has no close button), and focus returns to whatever had it
before. A sheet can also be dragged down or flicked closed, never only that (WCAG 2.5.7).

Motion: the dialog stays centred and enters with opacity and a slight scale over
`--sc-duration-slow` (280ms) with the strong ease-out; the sheet slides up on
`--sc-easing-drawer`. Both exit 20% faster (224ms). The scrim fades with them. Opened
from the keyboard it appears instantly (MOT-02); under reduced motion it only fades.

Session timeout: set `alert` and `countdown` (seconds). The time left shows as text,
updated every second, and is announced politely only once on open, at each whole minute
and at 30 and 10 seconds, never every second. `scCountdownEnd` fires at zero; expiring
never submits anything (TIME-03).

# sc-pagination

Moves between the pages of a long list: search results, payments, fines. Spec: `specs/sc-pagination.md`.

## Usage

```html
<sc-pagination page="7" total-items="1284" item-label="fine|fines" href-template="/en/fines?page={page}"></sc-pagination>
```

```html
<!-- Arabic page: six plural forms (zero|one|two|few|many|other) -->
<sc-pagination page="1" total-items="1284" item-label="مخالفة|مخالفة|مخالفتين|مخالفات|مخالفة|مخالفة" href-template="/ar/fines?page={page}"></sc-pagination>
```

- `total-items` shows the count: "Showing 121–140 of 1,284 fines" / "عرض 121 إلى 140 من 1,284 مخالفة". Arabic ranges always use a word, never a dash (LANG-22A). Digits are Latin, with a comma for thousands.
- Set `total-pages` directly, or let it follow from `total-items` and `page-size` (20).
- With `href-template` the pages are links and work without JavaScript. Without it they are buttons. Either way `scPageChange` fires with `{ page }`; `preventDefault()` stays on the page.
- Previous is left out on the first page and Next on the last. Below 600px: Previous, "Page 7 of 65", Next.
- Inside `sc-table`, put it in the `footer` slot.

### Styling hooks

Parts: `count`, `nav`, `list`.

# sc-search

A search box for a channel or a list of services.

## Usage

```html
<sc-search label="Search Dubai Now services" placeholder="Try “renew car registration” or “school fees”" action="/search"></sc-search>
```

```js
document.querySelector('sc-search').addEventListener('scSearch', (ev) => {
  ev.preventDefault();            // handle it in the page instead of going to `action`
  showResults(ev.detail.value);
});
```

- Give it a specific `label` ("Search Dubai Now services"). Hide it visually with `label-hidden` only where the context makes the purpose obvious, such as a hero that asks "What do you need to do?"; screen readers still read it.
- `placeholder` gives example queries. It disappears when typing, so never put instructions there.
- With `action`, submitting goes to that URL with `?q=…` (`name` changes the parameter) after `scSearch`, unless a listener cancels the event. Without `action`, handle `scSearch`.
- The button text defaults to "Search" ("بحث"); change it with `button-text` only for a more specific verb.

### Behaviour

v2 renders `<form role="search">` named by the label, a field box (radius 8, 1.5px `outline` edge, search icon at inline-start) holding a native `<input type="search">`, and a separate primary `sc-button type="submit"` 12px away (E1), all in light DOM (decision A2). Enter in the field submits through the button natively; `scSearch` carries the trimmed query. `focus()` on the host goes to the input, and the U1 focus ring wraps the field box. `size="l"` is the 64px hero search; the default `m` is 56px. Arabic-Indic digits typed into the query become Latin digits. The form is self-contained: don't put `sc-search` inside another `<form>`.

### Arabic

The field mirrors: icon on the right, button on the left. The default label and button read "بحث". Search terms are typed in either script; the field follows the page direction.

# sc-select

One choice from a list that's too long for radios, such as the issuing authority of a plate or an inspection centre. Use `sc-radio-group` when there are about 7 options or fewer: radios show every option without opening anything. Avoid selects for answers people know by heart (like a country); a text input with autocomplete is often easier.

## Usage

```html
<sc-select name="emirate" label="Issuing authority" value="dubai">
  <option value="dubai">Dubai</option>
  <option value="abu-dhabi">Abu Dhabi</option>
  <option value="sharjah">Sharjah</option>

# sc-spinner

A short inline wait, with a label saying what is loading. Inside a button, use `sc-button loading` instead.

## Usage

```html
<sc-spinner label="Checking your plate number"></sc-spinner>

# sc-status-tag

The status of an application, task or payment, in the words of the status vocabulary (Standard 9.6). Not interactive, and not announced when it changes.

## Usage

```html
<sc-status-tag tone="success">Paid</sc-status-tag>
<sc-status-tag tone="error">Action needed</sc-status-tag>
<sc-status-tag tone="warning">Expires in 15 days</sc-status-tag>
<sc-status-tag>In review</sc-status-tag>
```

| Tone | Icon | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `neutral` (default) | pending | Draft, Received, In review, Not approved, Withdrawn, Cancelled, Not started, In progress |
| `info` | hourglass | An informational state, where a service needs one. Standard 9.6 maps no status to it yet |
| `success` | check circle | Approved, Completed, Paid |
| `warning` | clock | Expires in {n} days |
| `error` | error | Action needed, Payment failed |

- Two or three words. Use the vocabulary, in both languages ("تم الدفع", "إجراء مطلوب").

# sc-table A table compares rows of the same kind of thing across a few attributes: a person's fines, their payments, the status of their permit applications. Each row is one thing; each column is one attribute. For the details of one thing, use `sc-summary-list`. Never use a table for layout. ## Usage ```html
Reference Date Offence Status Amount
F-2026-118204 14 Mar 2026 Speeding: 21 to 30 km/h over the limit Not paid AED 600.00
Showing 1–20 of 1,284 fines …Previous / Next…
Pay 2 fines ``` - **Scoped, not shadowed.** The component styles and enhances your native ``, so screen readers announce rows, columns and headers. Write `th scope="col"` headers and a `th scope="row"` as each row's first cell; it usually carries the row's link. Whole rows are never clickable. - **Caption** is required: `caption` writes a native `
`. Use `caption-hidden` when a heading straight above says the same thing. - **Column types** go on the header cell as `data-type` and set alignment, wrapping and figures for the whole column: `text` (wraps, never truncated), `reference` (nowrap, tabular; wrap the value in `sc-ltr`), `date`, `amount` (end-aligned, nowrap: the column grows instead), `status` (an `sc-status-tag`), `action` (end-aligned). Digits are Latin in both languages. - **Missing values:** leave the cell empty and the component writes a muted "None" (لا يوجد). Never a bare dash. - **Sorting:** add `data-sort` (optionally with a column key, `data-sort="amount"`) to a header. It becomes a button; Enter or a click cycles ascending and descending, one column at a time, sets `aria-sort` and announces "Sorted by Amount, highest first". The component only emits `scSort` with `{ column, direction }`: sort the data in the service (usually on the server) and re-render the rows. Sorting is never animated. - **Selection:** `selectable` adds a checkbox column at inline-start, identified by `tr[data-id]`, and a selection bar with the count, the total of the amount column (from `data-value`, or the cell text) and your `actions` slot. Label the checkboxes with `strings` ("Select fine {row}"). `selection-label` takes plural forms separated by `|` (English one|other; Arabic zero|one|two|few|many|other). `tr[data-selected]` preselects a row. `scSelectionChange` carries `{ ids }`. - **States:** `loading` shows 5 skeleton rows at the real column widths (the header stays). With no rows, the `empty` slot replaces the table: a `title-s` sentence and an optional next step ("You have no fines"; never "No data"). Add `filtered` for "No results" after a filter, which keeps the header. Put an `sc-callout tone="error"` with a "Try again" button in the `error` slot when the data can't load. Counts in the footer follow plural rules: "Showing 1 fine", never "1–1 of 1". - **Density:** `compact` (44px rows) is for staff tools with long lists. - **Below 600px** (the component's own width), `responsive="stack"` (default, up to about 6 columns) turns rows into cards: the row header is the title, the status sits at top inline-end, other cells become label and value pairs, the amount is the last line in `title-medium` and the action a full-width link row. `responsive="scroll"` keeps the table in a horizontal scroll region (focusable, named by the caption) with the row header sticky at inline-start and a shadow on the side with more content. A table wider than its container always scrolls rather than clipping. - **Links in cells** get a target of at least 44 × 44 px (an invisible hit area around the text) without changing the row height. - **Screen-reader context:** `class="sc-visually-hidden"` inside the table hides text visually: `View fine F-2026-118204`. - **Arabic:** everything mirrors: the first column and the checkboxes are on the right, amounts and actions align left, and the sort glyph sits after the label. Rows grow with the Arabic leading; nothing is fixed-height.

# sc-textarea

A longer answer that can run to several sentences: why a registration is being cancelled, a description of damage, a note for the inspector. For one line use `sc-text-input`.

## Usage

```html
<sc-textarea
  name="reason"
  label="Why are you cancelling the registration?"
  hint="For example, the vehicle was sold or exported"
  maxlength="200"
></sc-textarea>
```

Label, hint, `optional`, `error`, `required`, `heading-level`, rich slots and focus forwarding work exactly as in `sc-text-input` (see its readme). v2 renders a native `<textarea>` in light DOM (decision A2): it submits under `name`, resets and follows `<fieldset disabled>` natively. Enter adds a new line; it never submits.

### Character count

Set `maxlength` to show a count under the box: "You have 120 characters remaining" / "يتبقى لديك 120 حرفًا".

- **Typing isn't cut off.** People can type past the limit (no native `maxlength`), then the count says "You have 6 characters too many" in the error colour, the box gets the error border and `aria-invalid`, and the textarea reports a custom validity error with the same words (`setCustomValidity`), so the form won't pass `checkValidity()`. Editing down is easier than finding out the end of your text was silently dropped.
- **Announced politely, after a pause.** The visible count changes on every keystroke but is hidden from screen readers. A separate polite live region (`aria-live="polite"`, `aria-atomic`) is updated once typing has paused for one second, so screen reader users hear the count when they stop, not on every key.
- **Described up front.** "You can enter up to 200 characters" is part of the textarea's description, so the limit is heard on focus.
- **Arabic plurals.** The Arabic count uses the right form for the number (حرف واحد، حرفان، 3 أحرف، 120 حرفًا، 100 حرف), chosen with `Intl.PluralRules('ar')`. Characters are counted as people see them, so an emoji counts as one.

Use a limit only when there is a real one (a system field length). Size the box with `rows` to fit a typical answer.
